name: Synarchism
summary: Synarchism, as formulated by Alexandre Saint-Yves d'Alveydre, is a conservative, corporatist doctrine of 'joint rule' meant to replace anarchy and class struggle. Society is an organic hierarchy governed by three powers, education, justice and economy, with a spiritual direction and a federal European pact above the states.
scope: The doctrine of Saint-Yves d'Alveydre (Mission actuelle des souverains 1882, La France vraie 1887), as described in reference sources. It excludes the Vichy-era 'Pacte synarchique' conspiracy myth, LaRouchite polemic, the Mexican Catholic Synarchist movement and the sociological sense of synarchy in Qing China, all separate uses of the word. Many answers are low-confidence inferences, since he wrote in the 1880s.

sources.usedFor: Three elected chambers of education, justice and economy and three ministries.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Saint-Yves's three-council scheme assigns economic matters to a commerce council, but nothing in the sources addresses health care; a corporatist order could support it or leave it to communes.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Synarchy stresses class cooperation through corporate bodies rather than statutory wage floors, and the sources never mention wages, so adherents are not placed either way.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Saint-Yves wanted economic life ordered by a representative economic council and condemned a purely mechanical state, so unregulated markets would not be trusted; inferred, not stated.

public-ownership.rationale: Economic power is placed in a council of commerce and the communes, not in state ownership, and he called socialism antisocial; the inference is a mild no.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No source discusses taxation; class harmony and hierarchy point in opposite directions on this, so it is left neutral.

unions-good.rationale: Organised trade bodies are the basis of the economic chamber, so corporate organisation of workers fits, though independent adversarial unions are not what he proposed.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property is not discussed in the sources read; a hierarchical, conservative order suggests respect for it but the common-good emphasis tempers it.

regulate-corporations.rationale: An economic council that governs commerce implies organised regulation of economic actors, but the sources give no specifics.

cut-welfare.rationale: Synarchy aims at harmony between classes through institutions, so a hard welfare cut is unlikely; inferred only.

worker-ownership.rationale: Workers appear as a represented corporate estate, not as owners, and he rejected socialism as antisocial; inference.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Esoteric societies guard the state from behind the scenes in his scheme, but nothing addresses counterterrorism surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Never addressed by Saint-Yves; no principled inference from the sources.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed and anachronistic; his philosemitic writing does not tell us his view of legal limits on speech.

strong-leader.rationale: He criticised monarchs who rule through delegated power yet envisioned rule by three councils rather than one leader; a strongman bypassing institutions runs against the scheme.

state-harmful.rationale: He named anarchy as the great enemy and defined the state as the hierarchical organism of public powers, so the claim that the state is unnecessary and harmful is directly opposed.

empower-police-military.rationale: He wanted Europe to end the armed truce and disarm war, but nothing speaks to domestic police or military funding.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: A Christian-esoteric moral order makes legalisation unlikely, but the sources are silent; low-confidence inference.

decide-locally.rationale: The scheme has communes at the economic base but a European federal government above, so adherents favour layered rather than purely local decision-making.

rehabilitation.rationale: Justice has its own council but nothing on penal philosophy appears in the sources.

traditional-family.rationale: In Mission actuelle he describes family roles with the father holding Power and mother and grandfather Authority, treating the family as a model of ordered society.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from his Christian-hierarchical moral outlook; he did not address it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from Christian moral emphasis; not addressed in the sources.

more-religion-public.rationale: His third European council is a spiritual or 'theocratic' body charged with morals and education, and a metaphysical chamber binds the structure, giving religion a public role.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; nineteenth-century source with no such concept.

gender-social-construct.rationale: He assigns distinct family roles to father and mother, so a view of gender as mainly social construction is unlikely; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He aimed at a European federation and civilisational unity, not national culture as such, though tradition features in his idealised medieval Europe.

gradual-change.rationale: Change by sovereigns acting through public opinion and constitutional pact, as a counter to revolution, fits respect for institutions, though he did want a new European constitution.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from his federal European pact and general government of Christendom (s1, s3), which is supranational but not the UN.

free-trade.rationale: Commerce has its own council but his views on trade policy are not given in the sources read.

nation-first.rationale: He treated Europe's armed rivalry as the disease and sought a federal pact, so putting national interests above cooperation runs against his programme.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; he opposed armed rivalry but also saw sovereigns acting on Christian civilisational mission.

open-borders.rationale: Federal Europe is envisioned, but world open borders is not; weak inference.

limit-growth.rationale: His surviving writings concern constitutional and spiritual order, with no discussion of economic growth or ecology, so no stance can be inferred.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: His faith lies in spiritual and institutional reorganisation, not in technology; the sources do not address it.

revolution-justified.rationale: He read the Revolution as a push by dissatisfied middle classes and wanted change by sovereigns and opinion rather than by upheaval.

experts-over-public.rationale: His councils of instruction, justice and economy give weight to learned and trained elites, and his 'initiation and selection of the best' principle opposes demagogic mass suffrage.

central-planning.rationale: Economic power sits in a representative council of commerce rather than a state planning organ; no stated view on planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; economic autonomy of a corporate chamber is compatible with several ownership forms.

land-value-tax.rationale: The sources record no fiscal proposals, and his commerce council implies no particular tax doctrine, so neutral.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; hierarchy and inherited differentiation point mildly against heavy taxes.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade policy is absent from the sources; a council of commerce could favour either approach.

state-directs-investment.rationale: No source discusses investment policy; a corporate economic council could do so but the claim says state.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: He rejected socialism as antisocial and kept a commerce council, so an economy without wages and money is unlikely.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions do not appear in his writings, and the question postdates his work.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The Académie and Wikipedia both describe synarchy as a corporatist order of three representative bodies, with the economic chamber bringing employers and workers together.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Académie describes elected chambers with ministries drawn from them, and he opposed demagogic party politics, so a single ideological party is contrary to his scheme.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He describes sovereigns as having a mission to lead European federation and treats monarchy as having real functions, though he found many sovereigns merely nominal.

democracy-best.rationale: He distrusted 'suffrages démagogiques' and called republics monarchic machinery without a monarch, although his scheme had elected chambers.

direct-votes.rationale: He condemned demagogic suffrage and chose representation through functional chambers, so direct votes on laws run against it.

workers-councils.rationale: The scheme makes workers one stake within a commerce council among three, balanced by instruction and justice, not the basis of all power.

right-to-secede.rationale: He wanted European unification into a federal pact; secession is not discussed.

natural-rulers.rationale: The principle of initiation and selection of the best, and defence of hierarchy and social differentiation, mean some are suited to govern.

political-violence-never.rationale: He sought to disarm war and avoid revolution, but adherents' view on all political violence is not given.

war-builds-character.rationale: He denounced Europe's permanent armed rivalry as an immoral state of siege and wanted to disarm war.

separate-church-state.rationale: His third council is a church or spiritual body forming part of government, and the early Church is analysed as a model of the spiritual body of society.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: A Christian spiritual authority has a role in morals and education, but the sources do not say laws are drawn from scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Justice is one of three public powers with its own elected chamber, and the state is the hierarchical organism of public powers.

military-superiority.rationale: He wanted to end the armed truce, so superiority contests do not fit; adherents are not placed either way.

ethnic-nation.rationale: His vision is pan-European and Christian-civilisational, and his writing on Jews was favourable; no ethnic nationalism is documented.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The doctrine was framed to replace class struggle with cooperation between classes and to counter anarchism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: He defended social differentiation and hierarchy, so equal outcomes are not an aim.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The sources show no engagement with indigenous land rights, and his Eurocentric project gives nothing to infer from.

colonial-reparations.rationale: He criticised colonial rivalry as immoral, but reparations are not addressed.

civilizational-union.rationale: Mission actuelle proposes a federal pact and a general government of Christendom, an 'Empire de la Civilisation', uniting Europe's nations.

self-interest-moral.rationale: His ordering principle is association and harmony, not self-interest; inferred.

duties-before-rights.rationale: A hierarchical organic society with differentiated functions puts duty to the social whole first, but the sources do not state it directly.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: His esoteric cosmology has spiritual themes, but the sources do not tie them to the value of nature.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy is unaddressed in the sources read.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: He wrote in the 1880s as a proponent of ordered civilisation, and nothing indicates a critique of industrialism.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Rejects disruption of institutions in favour of ordered change, but technology as such is not discussed.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources give no basis for a stance on bodily technology.

algorithmic-government.rationale: He favoured councils of learned and spiritual authorities, not algorithms; anachronistic.

restore-past-order.rationale: His model draws on an idealised medieval Europe and an ancient synarchic government, so the recovery of a lost order is central.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He built a doctrinal system with an esoteric basis; pragmatic evaluation is not part of it.

direct-action.rationale: He sought reform through sovereigns and public opinion and condemned anarchy and revolutionary agitators.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed; he is a reformer by opinion and pact, not by prefigurative methods.

return-to-foraging.rationale: His programme is a sophisticated hierarchical civilisation with learned councils; foraging is contrary.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The doctrine is built on differentiated functions of society, like organs of a body.

distribute-by-need.rationale: He rejected socialism; the three-council order does not prescribe distribution by need.

production-for-use.rationale: No source discusses the purpose of production; his commerce council is not described as profit-oriented or not.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Class cooperation rather than exploitation theory is the premise, and socialism was dismissed as antisocial.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He called socialism 'antisocial' and aimed at inter-class collaboration; a class dictatorship is the opposite of his scheme.

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed; opposed to socialist collectivisation by inference.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: He attributed European war to diplomatic-military competition and sovereign rivalry, not to capitalism, but did not defend it either.

taxation-theft.rationale: He treated the state as a legitimate hierarchical organism with its own chambers and ministries.

harm-principle.rationale: A moral-spiritual body concerned with morals and education suggests the state concerns itself with more than harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Organic and corporate representation implies groups have standing; inferred.

conscription.rationale: His attention to armed rivalry is about ending the armed truce, not about how armies are manned.

exit-over-voice.rationale: A hierarchical state with representative councils has no place for exit as the main check.

state-as-business.rationale: He called the machine-like anonymous state a defect and the state a spiritual body of society.

positive-liberty.rationale: He wrote on institutional order, not on the philosophical meaning of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed, though his scheme gives a council of learning real power by design.

hereditarian-race.rationale: No source shows racial hierarchy in his writing, and he was favourable to Jews; weak inference.

organic-representation.rationale: Synarchy as described by both reference sources represents society through three functional chambers of education, justice and economy rather than through parties.

total-state.rationale: A three-power structure with a distinct spiritual council and economic autonomy is not a totalising state, but it is hierarchical.

national-rebirth.rationale: He sought a European renewal rather than a national one.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He opposed armed rivalry and sought a pact among European states.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: His design uses elected chambers and councils rather than personal oaths; his medievalism is not feudal-contractual in any source read.

bound-labor.rationale: Nothing in the scheme provides bound labour; he sought inter-class cooperation within an organised order, not serfdom.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Esoteric tradition holds that real knowledge exists and is guarded by initiates, contrary to the claim that knowledge merely reflects power.

universal-morality.rationale: Mission actuelle rests on universal Christian morality and ancient esoteric knowledge, with a spiritual council to hold moral principle.

single-common-good.rationale: The aim is harmony between groups through a unified structure, and the three councils work toward one social organism.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: His Mission des Juifs was favourable to Jews but the sources do not show any statehood position.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Nothing in the sources bears on diaspora citizenship.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language policy is absent from his writings as described by the sources.

workplace-democracy.rationale: He gave workers a representation in a commerce council but not a vote over firm management.

school-vouchers.rationale: He assigns education to a learned spiritual council; funding mechanisms are not discussed.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not discussed and is anachronistic for him.

economic-freedom.rationale: No source states his view; a structured economy under a council differs from laissez-faire.

rule-by-example.rationale: His esoteric order and an initiated, exemplary elite guard government, but the sources do not state this exact claim.

national-self-determination.rationale: He favoured European federation above states, so independent sovereign nation-states are not his aim.

force-without-un.rationale: He wanted peace through pact and opinion; the UN is anachronistic.

reason-over-faith.rationale: His doctrine is religious-esoteric, with a metaphysical chamber tying the structure together, so reason alone is not the sole guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The sources never discuss welfare entitlements or immigrants.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditions are absent from the sources.

class-collaboration.rationale: Both Wikipedia articles state that synarchy is a model of cooperation between social classes in place of class conflict.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: He valued inherited institutions, medieval Europe and ancient tradition and criticised only university archaism.

dominated-front.rationale: He sought cooperation, including East-West understanding in Keys of the Orient, rather than a front against the West.

workers-nation.rationale: He envisioned federal Europe and class cooperation rather than organising workers on a national basis.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Mission actuelle gives father and mother different functions in the family, but public life is not addressed.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury is not discussed in the sources, so adherents are not placed either way.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: His writing on Jews was favourable and nothing documented supports racial law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: He defined the state as the organism of public powers serving the whole society and sought class cooperation.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is anachronistic and unaddressed.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigration is not addressed; his project is a pan-European federation, which gives no basis for a direction.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not documented in his own thought; the conspiracy 'synarchy' is a later polemical use.

proportional-representation.rationale: Functional representation by sphere of society rather than by parties is the principle; party-list proportionality is not addressed.

national-mission.rationale: His mission is European and civilisational, not one nation's form of government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Given his positive account of family hierarchy, he would not frame society as systemically advantaging men.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He criticised demagogues and half-educated agitators seeking posts, but also held that sovereigns and councils should lead.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is not part of his documented thought, and the sources are silent.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Transitional justice is anachronistic and not covered in the sources.

night-watchman-state.rationale: His state has three chambers and three ministries over education, justice and economy, which is far more than a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: No documented support; his universalist Christian and Eastern-wisdom outlook points against it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equal moral worth is compatible with his Christian outlook, but he defended social differentiation and hierarchy, so he is left neutral.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not covered in the sources, which offer only his criticism of European colonial rivalry.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal-law questions are absent from the sources.

restrict-conversion.rationale: He favoured religious understanding among Jews, Christians and Muslims in Keys of the Orient.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Nothing in the sources concerns this Indian-specific policy, even though he wrote on India's role.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Education belongs to a spiritual council in his scheme, with moral instruction linked to the theocratic principle.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This concerns a socialist state, which his doctrine rejects, so it has no application.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The chambers are elected, but he distrusted mass suffrage and also grounded authority in a spiritual order, so adherents are split.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aims are not addressed in the sources.

population-transfer.rationale: His documented stance is of harmony and understanding between faiths, which excludes forced removal.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: He opposed war but did not state an absolute principle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: He condemned Europe's competitive armed rivalry and built a doctrine of association and harmony.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Party regulation is not discussed; his scheme gives parties no formal place.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: This is a republican-theory concept absent from the sources.

separated-powers.rationale: Synarchy divides authority among three chambers for education, justice and the economy (s2, s4), but they are coordinated functional bodies under a spiritual authority rather than mutual checks.

vanguard-party.rationale: He rejected socialism and revolutionary agitators.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Not addressed; Christian moral order might favour but sources are silent.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing policy is anachronistic and not discussed.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Not addressed; class cooperation might favour such restrictions but the sources do not say.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Neither population nor poverty causes are discussed in the sources.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The sources do not address ethnic diversity, and his documented stance on Jews and faiths was conciliatory without a stated cohesion theory.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Selection of the best and councils of learned and judicial persons conflict with sortition.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Emergency powers are not part of the described scheme.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not discussed; a commerce council could regulate prices but the sources do not say so.

party-controls-media.rationale: He distrusted partisan politics and a state-run machine; media control is not addressed.

party-commands-army.rationale: He did not envisage party rule and gave ministries to chambers.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship rules do not appear in the sources.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of representatives is not mentioned in the sources.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Representation is by function rather than party, so party discipline is not a feature.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: His central proposal in Mission actuelle is a European federal pact with a triple European council above states (s1), a binding supranational body, though the EU itself came a century later.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive power rests in three ministries emerging from the chambers, not a single head of state, but no armed-forces rule is given.

church-by-bishops.rationale: He analysed the Church's historical structure critically, but this governance question is not answered.

clerical-rule.rationale: A spiritual council holds one of three powers, but Mission actuelle also criticises the papacy as dominion-seeking, so he is not a clerical rule advocate.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Class collaboration and civic order, plus opposition to revolutionary agitation.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The spiritual council's concern with morals and education might point toward it, but the sources do not mention censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The sources give no terms or limits for office-holders.

recall-officials.rationale: Elected chambers and hierarchy rather than recall by voters; weak inference.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He wanted a federal pact replacing the armed truce; this is not the same as ending alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from rejection of radical socialism.

people-in-arms.rationale: He sought to disarm war; an armed citizenry is not part of his scheme.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Nothing in the sources contrasts rural and urban life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The sources show no concern with divided nations, as his focus is on all of Europe.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: He gave learned bodies a governing role and criticised only half-educated agitators.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: He praised Eastern wisdom and sought East-West understanding but also held a civilisational mission for Europe.

death-penalty.rationale: Penal sanctions are not discussed in the sources, though he assigned justice its own chamber.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from moral education under a spiritual council.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Education is assigned to a spiritual council, but the sources do not address evolution.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from his moral-spiritual concern for education and morals.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language rights are not addressed in the sources.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The sources discuss interfaith understanding, not legal exemptions from general law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: A hierarchical, organic order emphasises harmonised function over eccentricity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt is not discussed in the sources.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Decolonisation questions are anachronistic for him.

constituent-assembly.rationale: His constitutional change comes through sovereigns and pact on opinion, not a constituent assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Development strategy is not discussed in the sources.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign aid is anachronistic; the sources only show his European-federal focus.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons did not exist in his day, and no inference is available.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The executive in his scheme comes from the chambers rather than from a popular vote, so direct election of a head of state is not his model.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking is not discussed in the sources.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The sources give no position on territorial concessions.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: An organic order in which classes cooperate for a social whole suggests property serves society, but this is inferred.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is anachronistic and not addressed.

collective-defense.rationale: A federal European pact implies mutual security, but he sought disarmament of the armed truce, so the inference is weak.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He gave the spiritual power its own council independent of the state power, while criticising the papacy's political ambition.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: He wanted sovereigns to act above factions as guardians of a federal pact.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Secession is not covered in the sources.

region-keeps-system.rationale: A layered federal design allows autonomy but the specific claim is not discussed.

sacred-ruler.rationale: He found sovereigns largely nominal and placed authority in councils; divine descent is not claimed in the sources.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is not discussed in the sources.

character-from-environment.rationale: His esoteric tradition has its own anthropology, but the sources do not say how it treats nature versus nurture.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: His constitutional design binds government in three councils and ministries, and he criticised power exercised without structure.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic, with no support in the sources.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Synarchy combines elected chambers with learned, judicial and economic estates, a blended structure rather than rule by one.

leader-cult.rationale: A cult of one leader is opposed to government by three councils and his criticism of demagogy.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is anachronistic and absent from the sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The question presupposes a socialist state, which his doctrine does not envisage.

land-redistribution.rationale: Hierarchy and class cooperation point against seizure of estates.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee questions are not covered in the sources.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: He was against armed rivalries among states; irredentism is not part of his plan.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred from his interest in religious understanding among faiths (s3); apostasy is not discussed.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not addressed; not part of his documented framework.

common-currency.rationale: A federal European order points to common institutions, though no source mentions currency.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: His union is of Christendom's civilisation not of language-family kin peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority autonomy is not discussed in the sources, though federalism is his frame.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: No source addresses minority strategy in this sense.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: His account of history runs through spiritual and esoteric institutions and sovereigns, not economic base.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not discussed; a commerce council might organise rather than break up economic bodies.

no-bailouts.rationale: Public rescue of firms is not discussed in the sources.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Justice is an independent power with its own chamber, so courts are not subordinate to majority choice.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: He criticised colonial rivalry and aimed at federal European cooperation, not closed blocs.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Anachronistic; no source discusses trade agreements.

moral-incentives.rationale: A spiritual-moral council guiding social life implies weight on moral motive, but economic incentives are not discussed.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: He defended social differentiation and hierarchy.

history-own-civilization.rationale: His programme centres Europe's Christian civilisation and its mission, but school history is not discussed.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Mission actuelle speaks of a civilising mission of Europe and also criticises colonial rivalry, so adherents are split.

patriotic-education.rationale: He prioritised European and civilisational unity over national pride.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The sources do not address admissions or hiring policy.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation is not addressed in the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: He did not theorise capitalist crises in the sources read.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Imperial legacy politics is not addressed.

delink-world-market.rationale: Cooperation among states and federal order point against delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This is a Marxist-Leninist concept not found in his writing.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Organised corporate order points against laissez-faire discrimination.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rights charters are not discussed; the sources describe only a division of powers.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial borders are not discussed in the sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: The chambers are elected but he also valued monarchy; adherents' choice on head of state is unclear.

minority-veto.rationale: A hierarchical order of councils that decide for the whole cannot give vetoes to individuals.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Resistance to rulers is not discussed; he sought reform by sovereigns, not against them.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Power is divided among three chambers and ministries rather than one supreme parliament.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: A Christian hierarchical order with class cooperation suggests duties of the higher towards the lower.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: He was an activist who wrote to move sovereigns and opinion to act.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Frankfurt-school style cultural critique is absent from his writing.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony is a concept the sources do not connect to his work.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is absent from the sources and from his time.

native-born-offices.rationale: The sources do not address nativity rules for office.

party-own-road.rationale: The question concerns communist parties, which his doctrine does not include.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development theory is not addressed in the sources.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not applicable to his time, and later fascist associations are contested.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The sources offer no stance on fascism-versus-communism comparisons, and his own later fascist associations are disputed.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American history is outside what the sources cover.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Respect for inherited institutions makes preservation likelier; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender-policy questions of this kind are absent from the sources.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: He taught civilisational convergence of East and West yet gave Europe a distinct mission; split.

military-guardian-role.rationale: He wanted disarming of war; a guardian military is not in the sources.

paid-care-work.rationale: The sources do not discuss domestic labour beyond family roles.

filial-duty.rationale: Mission actuelle gives family a grandfather authority and a hierarchical structure; inferred respect for elders.

office-by-exam.rationale: Selection of the best and learned councils for instruction and justice fit selection by learning.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Representatives of functional chambers decide on behalf of their estate with authority, not as recallable delegates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not discussed in the sources.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not addressed; stability of property is inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The legislative role of the chambers is stated but a budget rule is not.

single-official-language.rationale: Language policy is not discussed in the sources.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anti-discrimination law is anachronistic and absent.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: He wanted to disarm the competition between states, not fuel it.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: He sought a voluntary federal pact based on opinion.

corporate-influence.rationale: Lobbying and campaign finance are not discussed in the sources.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population policy is absent from the sources.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local housing restrictions are not addressed.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employment policy is not discussed in the sources.

democratic-peace.rationale: He doubted popular government and sought peace through sovereigns' pact, so he did not make this claim.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: An ordered hierarchy of public powers presumes obligation to its law.

non-intervention.rationale: He envisioned a federal European authority acting above states and Christendom's general government, so absolute non-intervention is not his principle.

industrial-unions.rationale: The sources mention organised economic bodies but not union structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: His Mission des Juifs was favourable to Jews; the conspiracy 'synarchy' is a later polemic, not his view.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from his family model and Christian outlook (s1, s3); marriage law is not discussed.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Esoteric societies working behind the scenes are part of his scheme, so openness is not a priority.

local-production.rationale: The sources show no view on economic localism.

informal-organisation.rationale: His design is a formal, hierarchical, institutionalised order.

national-law-over-international.rationale: His federal pact places a European body above states.

religious-nation.rationale: Christian civilisation is the frame but he aimed at religious understanding among faiths; national religion is not his definition.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not addressed in his writings; the term synarchy in Qing studies is a separate usage.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism is not discussed in the sources.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The sources do not discuss the property distinction in this form.

defeat-communism.rationale: He called socialism antisocial but wrote before communist states; the Mexican strand opposed the revolutionary left.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public-service delivery is not discussed in the sources.

religion-illusion.rationale: Mission actuelle treats religion and the spiritual power as the foundation of social order, crediting Christ's moral force with checking despotism.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: He did not use a historical-materialist schema, and the sources show no view on capitalism's historical role.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The sources do not link gender and economic order.

socialized-care.rationale: His family model gives family roles to mothers and fathers, inferred against public replacement.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not mentioned in the sources.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not discussed in the sources.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Not a federation of small communes; he proposed communes only as the economic layer of a European structure.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He rejected socialism as antisocial and sought a corporatist third structure, but never framed it as a third way.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The sources do not address land claims, though his Mission des Juifs was favourable to Jews without a stated territorial claim.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic; his documented views on Jews were favourable, and nothing supports denial.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Sexual criminal law is not addressed in the sources.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He sought concert through opinion and elected chambers rather than repression.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Not addressed; interfaith understanding points against, Christian order for.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Mission actuelle criticises colonial rivalry among European powers as immoral, which counts against governing colonies for the metropole's benefit.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not applicable and counter to his interfaith vision.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: He sought reform by sovereigns and pact, not by rebellion on religious grounds.

participatory-democracy.rationale: He distrusted mass politics; participation goes through functional chambers.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectionality is outside his period and the sources.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his family model.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Christian moral order.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: He positioned synarchy as transcending anarchy and class conflict by combining all strata; not stated as left-right.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxian alienation does not appear in the sources.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Keys of the Orient proposed understanding among Jews, Christians and Muslims.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: His authority principle lies in a spiritual power and a metaphysical chamber above the structure, but he is not simply a divine-right theorist.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: A religiously informed public order is unlikely to ban such dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace law of this kind is anachronistic and absent.

social-market-economy.rationale: A managed economy under an economic council combined with class cooperation parallels a social-market idea, but not stated.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He wanted to disarm war but not stated as abolition.

rich-first.rationale: Development sequencing is not discussed in the sources.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Bloc politics are anachronistic; his federal-European focus gives no clear direction.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Not addressed; he regarded monarchy sympathetically but succession is not discussed.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Credit and banking are not discussed in the sources.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: International lending conditions are anachronistic and not addressed.

property-franchise.rationale: He wanted an electorate organised by function rather than wealth.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist theory is outside his thought and the sources.

reification.rationale: This is a Marxist concept absent from his writing.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The sources do not address press ownership.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: A legislative power in elected chambers with a separate judicial power implies law by announced rules, but not stated.

racial-franchise.rationale: Inferred: his electoral model is functional and describes no racial qualification (s3).

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic, and he prefers functional representation.

open-government-data.rationale: Not a feature of a system guarded by esoteric societies.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The sources show only his interest in interfaith understanding, not marriage law.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from his documented favourable stance towards Jews (s3); boycotts are not discussed.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition is not part of his scheme of selected, learned and elected bodies.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: He reinterpreted Christianity esoterically but the claim is about religious law; split.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The sources do not discuss wealth concentration and liberty.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Mission actuelle grounds public order in a spiritual power and treats religion as a social foundation, opposing state atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Justice is a core public power in his scheme.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Joint rule among communities and functions is the meaning of synarchy as shared rule.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The sources do not compare charity and state aid; a spiritual council might take a role, but nothing is stated.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from his scheme of expert councils of education, justice and economy and hostility to demagogic suffrage; term limits on elected office are not discussed.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from his rejection of universal suffrage in favour of hierarchical, competence-based councils; delegable voting is not discussed.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses extinction risk; his federal European pact aims at peace, which could support it, but he wrote in the 1880s.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from his hierarchical, organic social model and his spiritual direction by an initiated elite; female clergy are not discussed.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from his conservative, hierarchical view of family and society as organic order; marital authority is not directly stated in the sources read.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred: Saint-Yves's organic, hierarchical society of corporate bodies gives little place to individual political rights for outsiders.

rent-control.rationale: His economic council could regulate rents but nothing in the sources addresses housing.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: his corporatist order protects established property and professions, and the sources do not mention intellectual property.

uniformed-youth.rationale: His education power might organise youth but the sources do not discuss uniformed movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic; nuclear weapons postdate the doctrine and nothing can be inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed; his European federal pact would regulate military questions above the states.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources do not address genocide recognition.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine seeks harmony of labour and capital through corporate organisation in place of class struggle.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from his Christian, conservative order; the sources never discuss it.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine treats France and Europe as organic historical communities, as in La France vraie.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred: a conservative, hierarchical doctrine of organic natural order; the sources are silent on sex and gender.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from his conservative, organic view of society; the sources do not discuss feminism.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The sources do not address martyr cults; the doctrine is spiritual but not nationalist in that sense.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The doctrine places a spiritual direction above the three powers of education, justice and economy, so politics is ordered by spiritual authority.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: No evidence the doctrine addresses diaspora homelands.

culture-before-state.rationale: Education is one of his three powers, but the sources do not rank culture before the state.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred: a traditional Christian esoteric framework; the sources do not discuss gendered language for God.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred: a hierarchical, traditional framework gives scripture authority over modern criteria; unaddressed in sources.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The doctrine is a federal, Europe-wide order and does not address ethnic economic preference.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: His federal pact respects historical states and regions, but the sources do not discuss merging regions by people.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from Saint-Yves's economic council of self-governing corporate bodies, which implies autonomous trade organisation, though he never wrote about modern unions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Synarchy rejects class struggle and rests on an organic hierarchy of three powers, so working-class rule is not its test of a good society.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Sources never mention public services; a corporatist order could support public or corporate provision.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from the three-council structure with a federal pact above states, which implies several bodies of government rather than one elected chamber.

municipal-property.rationale: Sources describe an economic council but not who owns productive property; adherents are not placed either way.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Synarchy proposes a federal European pact and communal bodies, but with a hierarchical direction from above, which cuts against delegates who only coordinate.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from its corporatist, conservative stress on stable class cooperation; the sources do not mention family wages.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Nineteenth-century doctrine with no stated view on drug regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Nineteenth-century doctrine with no stated view on life-extension research.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on financial privacy.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on online anonymity.

person-over-state.rationale: Saint-Yves's organic hierarchy gives the social body priority, yet his doctrine also invokes Christian personal dignity; sources do not settle it.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Saint-Yves set a spiritual direction at the head of society, with education and religious authority as one of the three powers.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The sources describe a federal European pact but not how the national legislature relates to regional powers.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on genetically engineered crops.

dense-cities.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on urban density.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred from Saint-Yves's universalist, European-federal aim of harmony among peoples, which does not organise politics by race.

racial-pride.rationale: The sources show no engagement with racial pride; the doctrine is about social order and a European pact.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from Saint-Yves's aim of a European pact replacing rivalry and war between states.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Saint-Yves proposed a federal European pact above the states and organic hierarchy by function, not nations defined by language; inferred, since sources do not discuss this criterion.

communal-electorates.rationale: His three-council system gives representation by corporate function and body, a form of group representation, not common individual voting; inferred by analogy, as religious electorates are not mentioned.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Nothing in the sources attributes partition plots to foreign powers; the Vichy-era conspiracy myth is excluded by scope.

free-public-college.rationale: Education is one of his three powers, but sources do not say whether it should be free; inferred as unaddressed.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Anachronistic: a corporatist order would regulate through its councils rather than pricing pollution; inferred, as 1880s sources never discuss it.

future-generations.rationale: Anachronistic; sources do not address environmental stewardship and a conservative organic order could support either view.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Saint-Yves wrote on a role for women in his scheme, but the sources here do not state a view on weighting women's typical values; treated as unaddressed.

arms-reduction.rationale: The federal European pact is meant to replace war between states with joint rule; inferred disarmament leaning, not stated.

open-diplomacy.rationale: His esoteric, initiatic conception of government and rule by an elite spiritual direction suggests tolerance for confidential dealings; inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: Economic matters belong to his commerce council, but sources do not address capital movement; unaddressed.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Saint-Yves's ordered, hierarchical state under three powers implies a public monopoly of arms, but the sources do not discuss it; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: An organic hierarchy ordered by the sovereigns' mission and a European pact for peace would treat refusal of orders as disorder; inferred from the conservative order he defended.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The corporatist economic council representing trades implies collective negotiation of conditions, though no source states it; inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses tax credits; a corporatist order could use them or leave support to trade bodies.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The sources describe a commerce council but give no fiscal rules; inferred as unsettled.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Saint-Yves proposed a European federal pact above the states but nothing on developing countries, which he did not address.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Synarchy is meant to replace anarchy and class struggle with ordered rule through the existing sovereigns, so smashing the state conflicts with it; inferred.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Synarchism prescribes a specific three-power blueprint, so a no-blueprint stance conflicts with it.

nature-as-capital.rationale: He wrote in the 1880s and the sources do not address ecosystems as capital.

sacred-nation.rationale: Synarchy treats society as an organic whole under spiritual direction, which suggests agreement with an enduring national community, though his focus was a European federation; inferred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: His corporatist order would not make debt relief a state function; the sources do not address it, so inferred mild disagreement.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The sources do not address regional exploitation; his federal scheme gave regions a voice but no stated theory of exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Saint-Yves grounded society in a divinely ordered hierarchy and the Christian-derived social order, which fits a fixed human nature; inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: His education power implies a public role in culture, but independence from government is not addressed.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Saint-Yves's synarchy rests on an initiatory tradition behind all religions, with a spiritual direction above the state; inferred from that esoteric universalism rather than a quoted line.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred: a corporatist organic order with an economy council would regulate agriculture and credit to protect producers; nothing in the sources discusses farm prices.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from his insistence on state strength and a European pact of armed sovereigns, not from any text on nuclear arms.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred: synarchy seeks to end class struggle through joint rule and functional councils, so a class party would be opposed; not stated directly.

ban-fgm.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a conservative order built on education and justice powers that would likely condemn mutilation, though he did not address it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Saint-Yves's organic hierarchy did not address inheritance law and a conservative corporatist order could go either way.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred from his pan-European cultural unity and linguistic scholarship; the sources do not discuss this question.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses liability law; a corporatist order could prefer council regulation or courts.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: He envisaged councils of educated and professional bodies, not customary chiefs; no source addresses it, so inferred as split.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Anachronistic; an organic hierarchy ranks social order above liberty, but environmental protection is not discussed.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred: a hierarchical, justice-focused order favours firm law, but he left no detail on sentencing.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred: an organic society with a shared civilisation would expect assimilation, though the sources do not address migration.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from the corporatist model of functional bodies for education, justice and economy, which implies organised trades rather than purely optional membership; the sources do not discuss unions.

voter-id.rationale: Saint-Yves attacked demagogic suffrage but proposed elected functional chambers; nothing in the sources addresses identification at the polls.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from his spiritual direction of society and his analysis of the Church as a guiding authority, which favours a hierarchy of religious authority over strict legal equality.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: He opposed demagogic universal suffrage and revolution in favour of an organic hierarchy, so competitive elections alone would not make a government legitimate to him.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from his conservative, Church-respecting view of family and organic society; he did not address the question directly.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The internet is anachronistic; his hierarchical order would allow authority to keep order but he stressed harmony, so adherents are split.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses welfare design; a corporatist economy council could favour either targeted or unified schemes.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred only: he wrote in the 1880s and his chambers were organised by function and family, with no documented position on women's political rights.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from his respect for the Church and its role in family and society; he did not treat religion as oppressing women.

race-social-construct.rationale: He wrote on civilisation and races of the Orient and Europe in 1880s terms; there is no documented stance on the modern constructionist claim.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from his conservative organic hierarchy, which favours family and functional bodies over dedicated state equality agencies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Saint-Yves wrote in the 1880s and the sources do not discuss first-claim ownership; his economic council could regulate property either way.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from his plan for a European federal pact above the states with arbitration among sovereigns; he wrote before international criminal courts existed.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred: his doctrine is esoteric and initiatory, treating religion through hidden spiritual direction, not literal scriptural reading.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred: he proposed an organic hierarchy of social bodies, and the sources do not address gender equality or Indigenous self-government.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: his corporatist order rejects class struggle and collectivist socialism, though it keeps an economic council.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred: his scheme builds councils upward from lower bodies in a hierarchy, in which higher authorities are chosen by delegation, though the sources do not detail the method.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred and split: he assigns spiritual direction to an initiatory elite rather than a state church, so a legally privileged national church is not clearly part of it.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from his federal, organic-community model with self-governing bodies below a European pact.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed; sources do not address plebiscites.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed in the sources.

simple-living.rationale: Unaddressed; the doctrine concerns the structure of government, not lifestyles.

equal-conscription.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed in the sources.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Synarchy is a European federal scheme and the sources say nothing on a spiritual tie to a national homeland; inferred as neutral from its supranational focus.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Synarchy is a legalist, hierarchical order of justice councils, so summary killing without trial is inferred to be contrary to it; the sources do not address it.

close-ties-china.rationale: Saint-Yves wrote in the 1880s about a European pact and never discussed China, so no position can be inferred.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The doctrine aims at a European federation above the states and the sources do not discuss kin minorities abroad; no position is inferred.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The sources do not discuss resource ownership; a corporatist economic council could take either view.

self-ownership.rationale: Synarchy treats society as an organic hierarchy of corporate bodies rather than sovereign individuals, so individualist self-ownership is inferred to sit uneasily with it.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Taxation policy is not addressed in the sources; economic matters are left to a commerce council, so no position is inferred.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Social spending design is not addressed in the sources; no position can be inferred.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Synarchy builds government on organised bodies (three councils), so bypassing intermediary groups is inferred to be contrary to it, though the sources do not discuss leaders.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The sources do not address business privileges; a corporatist order sits between privilege and equal rules, so no position is inferred.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Saint-Yves framed the Church as a guiding spiritual power in his council scheme, so excluding denominations from politics is inferred to be disfavoured.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Synarchy joins an esoteric, traditional spiritual direction with modern organised economy and education; inferred from that blend, not stated on this question.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Divorce law is not addressed in the sources and the doctrine's treatment of the family is not clear enough to infer a position.

national-resource-control.rationale: His project is a European federal pact above states, so national resource control is not addressed; no position is inferred.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Saint-Yves proposed an organic hierarchy of three councils but sources do not address just distribution; inferred as split between process and fairness.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses financial taxes; the 1880s doctrine pre-dates currency markets of this kind.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Saint-Yves wrote in the 1880s and the sources do not address this question; inferred.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Synarchy grounds authority in a spiritual and moral order above rulers, so a law violating it would plausibly not bind; inferred.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Anachronistic for an 1880s doctrine; no source addresses automation.

multipolar-world.rationale: Saint-Yves proposed a federal European pact of states rather than one dominant power; inferred from that scheme.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the economic council scheme gives no theory of value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Synarchy stresses class cooperation and a federal Europe above states; the link between patriotism and workers is not documented.

material-over-identity.rationale: Synarchy rejects class struggle but does not address left strategy; inferred as split.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Synarchy was framed against anarchy and class struggle and favours a corporatist order; inferred that communist party rule would be rejected.

missingStatements.text: Society should be governed by councils representing education, justice and the economy as separate branches.
missingStatements.rationale: The three-chamber functional structure is the defining institutional proposal of synarchy.
missingStatements.declined: Synarchy-specific institutional scheme (three functional chambers); no other ideology would meaningfully take a side.

missingStatements.text: Spiritual and esoteric bodies should guide government from behind the scenes.
missingStatements.rationale: Saint-Yves held that initiatory societies, like medieval Rosicrucians, safeguard the state as oracles.
missingStatements.declined: Synarchy-specific esoteric doctrine; not worth a bank slot.

notes: Primary reading covered only the first part of Mission actuelle des souverains; La France vraie was not accessed in full text. Positions on economics and social policy are largely inferred.
